litematic-printer-ling.config.serverSafe: One-key switch between the conservative public-server preset and the single-player performance preset. On: applies the three custom safe values below plus RTT adaptive. Off: performance preset (0 ticks / 8 blocks / unlimited breaks / RTT adaptive off). The preset is only applied when the switch flips; if you change place interval, blocks per tick or breaks per tick while it is on, safe mode turns itself off and keeps your values.
litematic-printer-ling.config.safePlaceI: Place interval in ticks used while server safe mode is on. Default 2 (0.1 s). Raise to 3-5 if the server swallows placements.
litematic-printer-ling.config.safePlacem: Maximum blocks placed per tick while server safe mode is on. Default 3 (about 30 blocks/s with a 2 tick interval).
litematic-printer-ling.config.safeBreaks: Maximum blocks broken per tick while server safe mode is on. Default 8.
litematic-printer-ling.config.iterationD: Which direction candidates are consumed first for mine/fill/cover/fluid/bedrock. Nearest-first (default) spreads around the player; the other options sweep monotonically along one axis, e.g. bottom-up for shafts or north-to-south for large floors.
litematic-printer-ling.message.server_sa: Server safe mode: ON (custom safe preset applied)
Server safe mode: OFF (performance preset applied)
Server safe mode: turned off automatically (you changed a rate value)
litematic-printer-ling.config.bedrock.de: Run an internal bedrock-breaking state machine inside the selection. Requires pistons, redstone torches, slime blocks and a pickaxe that can instant-mine pistons.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakBlack:
Prohibit print-mode auto-breaking from handling blocks in this list.
This mainly affects automatic cleanup of wrong/extra blocks during printing and does not affect mining mode.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Block state matching is also supported, example: §bminecraft:wheat[age=7]§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakBlock:
Number of blocks mining mode can process per game tick. Higher values mean more blocks mined each time, provided they can be broken within one tick.
Set to §b0§r for no limit.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakCheck: Whether to skip unbreakable blocks (blocks with hardness of -1). If only the hardness of certain blocks has been modified on the server side, you can disable this option.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakCoold: Cooldown time after breaking the same position in mining mode (in game ticks). Retry only after the cooldown ends.
litematic-printer-ling.config.bedrockInt:
Interval between bedrock launch windows (in game ticks).
With interval 10 and throughput 6, each window may start up to 6 new chains; existing machines continue every tick.
Higher values slow new-window admission.
litematic-printer-ling.config.bedrockBlo:
Maximum targets submitted and advanced in one execution window.
The interval controls how often that window opens; active-target capacity follows this value.
Higher values are faster, but also increase cleanup pressure and machine overlap risk.
litematic-printer-ling.config.bedrockAll:
Allow bedrock breaking to use horizontal piston layouts when no vertical layout is available.
Disabled by default to avoid horizontal look-settle delays slowing multi-layer jobs; when enabled, exposed vertical layouts are still preferred.
litematic-printer-ling.config.bedrockMul: Use server RTT and block-update timing to extend confirmation grace and back off retries for the same target. RTT 0 keeps the current singleplayer speed.
litematic-printer-ling.config.bedrockWhi:
Additional blocks allowed into the bedrock-breaking state machine.
Can input block ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:obsidian§r §bobsidian§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:dragon_immune§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §ldeepslate,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakInter:
Interval between mining-mode break actions (in game ticks).
Set to 0 for no interval (may cause server lag), recommended to set to 1-5 to balance speed and performance.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakLimit:
Block filtering rules for print-mode auto-breaking.
§dNo Limit§r: No restriction on print auto-breaking
§dWhitelist§r: Only allow auto-breaking for blocks in the whitelist
§dBlacklist§r: Prohibit auto-breaking for blocks in the blacklist
§lNote:§r This only affects print-mode auto-breaking and does not affect mining mode.§r

Source of print auto-break rules:
§dTweakeroo Preset§r: Use Tweakeroo mod's break restriction rules
§dCustom§r: Use the printer's custom print auto-break rules.
This only affects print-mode auto-breaking and does not affect mining mode.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakProgr: When delayed confirmation is enabled, send STOP after continuous breaking reaches this percentage and wait for the server update. When disabled, keep the vanilla 0.7 threshold behavior. Higher values are safer; lower values are more aggressive.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakUseDe: Use the modern delayed-confirmation queue for both printing and mining. Targets wait for a server block update and are released on timeout; the legacy same-tick START/STOP path is never used. Disabled keeps the current continuous-breaking behavior.
litematic-printer-ling.config.breakWhite:
Only allow print-mode auto-breaking to handle blocks in this list.
This mainly affects automatic cleanup of wrong/extra blocks during printing and does not affect mining mode.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Block state matching is also supported, example: §bminecraft:wheat[age=7]§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematic-printer-ling.config.category.b: Low-level break protocol and progress settings shared by mining and other break flows
litematic-printer-ling.config.category.s: Toggles for relaxed restrictions, material retrieval, unusual compatibility, and environment-dependent behavior
litematic-printer-ling.config.checkPlaye:
When enabled, printer only processes blocks within player's block interaction range.
Positions beyond interaction distance will not perform operations to avoid cross-distance operations being detected by servers.
If you're playing on servers that allow cross-distance interaction, you can disable this option.
litematic-printer-ling.config.closeAllMo: Close all working modes; if currently running in single mode, will automatically revert to printing mode.
litematic-printer-ling.config.easyPlaceP:
Use Servex's easy place protocol to handle block placement correction during printing.
§lNote:§r This feature only works in single-player or on servers with Servux installed.
litematic-printer-ling.config.excavateBl:
Prohibit mining blocks in this list.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Block state matching is also supported, example: §bminecraft:wheat[age=7]§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematic-printer-ling.config.excavateLi:
Block filtering rules for mining mode.
§dNo Limit§r: No restriction on any block mining
§dWhitelist§r: Only allow mining blocks in whitelist
§dBlacklist§r: Prohibit mining blocks in blacklist
§lNote:§r When using Tweakeroo mining limit presets, this setting will not take effect.§r

Source of mining limit rules:
§dTweakeroo Preset§r: Use Tweakeroo mod's mining limit rules
§dCustom§r: Use printer's custom mining limit rules.
litematic-printer-ling.config.excavateWh:
Only allow mining blocks in this list.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Block state matching is also supported, example: §bminecraft:wheat[age=7]§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Where "c" represents contains matching, prioritizing pinyin or direct matching.
litematic-printer-ling.config.fill.desc: Within the selection range, place blocks configured in §6Fill Block List§r.
litematic-printer-ling.config.fillBlockL: Block list used by filling mode, configuration rules consistent with "Basic Block List".
litematic-printer-ling.config.fillBlockM:
Block selection mode for filling.
§dBlock List§r: Use blocks in configured list
§dHeld Item§r: Use currently held block in main hand
litematic-printer-ling.config.fillModeFa: Facing settings when filling blocks. For example, placing upper slabs or lower slabs.
litematic-printer-ling.config.fillSelect:
Working selection range rules for filling mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute filling within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematic-printer-ling.config.fluid.desc: At lava sources and water sources positions, default place blocks configured in §6Fluid Replacement Block List§r.
List of liquids that need to be replaced, can only input liquid IDs, example: §bminecraft:water§r.
litematic-printer-ling.config.fluidModeF: When enabled, flowing liquids will also be treated as targets needing filling and replacement.
litematic-printer-ling.config.fluidRepla:
Block list for filling liquids. Can input item ID or displayed name, example: §bminecraft:sand§r §bsand§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:sand§r.
litematic-printer-ling.config.fluidSelec:
Working selection range rules for fluid removal mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute fluid removal within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematic-printer-ling.config.mine.desc: Mine all non-liquid blocks within selection range.
litematic-printer-ling.config.mineTrench: Before mining, fills fluids inside the selection and in blocks immediately beside both sides of a straight selection using the configured blocks. Disabled by default.

Blocks used to fill fluids in trench mode. Defaults to sand. Supports item IDs, display names and #tags.
For the Nether, use only minecraft:cobblestone. Missing listed materials waits for resupply without falling back to sand. An empty list or no matching blocks disables filling.
litematic-printer-ling.config.mineSelect:
Working selection range rules for mining mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute mining within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection (default)
litematic-printer-ling.config.modeSwitch:
§dSingle Mode§r: Only run one working mode at a time
§dMulti Mode§r: Can run multiple working modes simultaneously
§lNote:§r Need to reopen settings menu after switching to see mode change effects.§r
litematic-printer-ling.config.openScreen: Hotkey to open printer settings menu (the page you're currently viewing).
litematic-printer-ling.config.placeBlock:
Number of blocks that can be placed per game tick. Higher values mean more blocks placed each time.
Set to §b0§r for no limit.
litematic-printer-ling.config.placeCoold:
Cooldown time after placing blocks at the same location (in game ticks). Retry placement operation only after cooldown ends.
§c§lDo not set to 0 unless necessary, otherwise it will cause placing extra blocks, inability to place correctly and other issues!§r
litematic-printer-ling.config.placeRttAd:
Automatically raise the placement interval to at least one round-trip (your ping) so a placement is not sent before the server confirms the previous one.
Reduces misplaced/ghost blocks on servers, especially with high latency.
Uses your tab-list ping; has no effect in singleplayer/LAN (ping 0).
litematic-printer-ling.config.placeRttSa: Use this percentage of the measured RTT as the minimum interval. 100 = exactly one round-trip. Higher is safer but slower; lower is faster but riskier.
litematic-printer-ling.config.placeInAir: Ignore block support requirements and place blocks directly in air positions (applicable to unsupported decorative blocks).
litematic-printer-ling.config.tweakerooA: When enabled, players with build permission can also pass Tweakeroo's angel block placement check. This usually affects survival mode.\nWhen disabled, Tweakeroo's original creative-only behavior is preserved.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printSortS: When enabled, prioritize placement faces that are closer to the player's view and usually easier to click.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printSortT: When enabled, prioritize print targets matching the held block, closer to the view direction, and closer to the player.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printRepai: When enabled, the printer checks RailShape after placing rails and will break and retry up to 3 times if neighbor updates bend them incorrectly. This is a client-side best-effort repair and cannot fix every vanilla-unstable shape.
litematic-printer-ling.config.placeInter:
Interval time for placing blocks (in game ticks).
May automatically add delays to avoid placement errors for some special blocks.
Setting to 0 may cause poor performance on servers with packet restrictions.
Not recommended to set to 0 when printing redstone mechanisms.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printAutoF:
Automatically fill compostable items into composters to generate bone meal.
(§lWarning: This operation will consume compostable items in inventory!§r)

Compostable items used for automatic composter filling.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:wheat§r §bwheat§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#compostable§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching (prioritizing pinyin/direct matching), example: §lwheat,c§r.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printAutoS: When enabled, if stripped logs are not in inventory, will first place normal logs, then automatically strip them with axe to save manual operation time.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printAutoT: When printing note blocks, automatically tune note blocks to the pitch specified in schematic.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printBreak:
Automatically break extra blocks that don't exist in schematic during printing.
Affected by the print auto-break restriction settings.

Automatically break blocks that completely mismatch the schematic during printing.
Affected by the print auto-break restriction settings.

Automatically break blocks whose type matches the schematic but whose state differs.
Connection states and some blocks affected by world updates are skipped. Disabled by default.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printFalli: When enabled, will check if blocks below falling blocks match schematic, and skip placement if incorrect.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printForce: Automatically maintain sneaking state during printing process.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printReser:
Prevent the printer from performing an action that would reduce the current material below the configured reserve.
Only affects printing mode; damageable tools, manual actions, and other work modes are unaffected.
Minimum quantity to keep for each actual printing material. Consumption pauses at the reserve and resumes after the material is replenished.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printIceFo: Generate water source blocks through "place ice → break ice" method to achieve water source printing.
In replacement mode, replace specified source blocks with target blocks in selection area.
Can input source block ID/name and target block ID/name (separated by English colon), example: §bminecraft:stone:minecraft:oak_planks§r §bstone:oak_planks§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#logs:minecraft:oak_planks§r (replace all logs with oak planks).
litematic-printer-ling.config.printRepla: Directly overwrite blocks in list without skipping processing or breaking.
When printing dead coral, if no dead coral in inventory, use live coral as substitute; if both exist, will prioritize using dead coral.

Block list that can be directly overwritten during printing (without breaking original blocks).
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching, example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printSafel: Check if suitable for placement before placing observers to avoid accidentally triggering your machines and causing disasters.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printSelec:
Working selection range rules for printing mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute printing within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection (default)
When enabled, will skip blocks in the list during printing.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printSkipL:
Block list skipped during printing. Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching, example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printerAut: Automatically disable printer when player dies to avoid misoperations after respawning.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printerRen: Only render schematic blocks whose items are in the inventory, including shulker box contents.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printerIte:
Area shape for printer block iteration:
§dCube§r: Cube with §6§lWork Radius§r as edge length (recommended value: 3)
§dSphere§r: Sphere with §6§lWork Radius§r as radius (recommended value: 6)
§dOctahedron§r: Octahedron with §6§lWork Radius§r as edge length (recommended value: 6)
litematic-printer-ling.config.printerLag: used as the upper limit for lag detection.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printerMod:
Printer's core work mode:
§dPrinting§r: Restore blocks in projection blueprint (including direction, state and other properties)
§dMining§r: Mine blocks within selection range (except fluids)
§dBedrock Breaking§r: Break bedrock within selection range using game mechanics (only available for 1.19+ with Bedrock Miner mod installed)
§dFluid Removal§r: Fill liquids in projection selection with specified blocks
§dFilling§r: Fill projection selection with blocks

§lNote:§r Except for §dPrinting§r mode, operation ranges of other modes are all within projection selection, can also be changed by adjusting §6§lSelection Type§r of each mode.
litematic-printer-ling.config.printerSel:
Working selection range rules for printing mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute printing within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematic-printer-ling.config.quickShulk: Directly take needed materials from shulker boxes in inventory for quick item retrieval.
Cooldown time for quick shulker function (in game ticks). Some plugin servers have cooldown restrictions for this function. Set to 0 to disable cooldown.

§dSimulate Click§r: Right-click shulker box slot in inventory to open (requires server plugin support)
§dInvoke Mod§r: Directly invoke QuickShulker mod to open (requires installation on both sides for normal use)
litematic-printer-ling.config.remoteTake: When Chest Tracker is installed, retrieve missing materials only from containers explicitly cached inside the current Litematica selection. The cache is local and world/dimension-scoped; right-clicking an item in the Chest Tracker list also uses this allow-list. Mixed shulker boxes are restored to their source slot when possible.
litematic-printer-ling.config.voidWareho:
When a material runs out, request a full stack from the server-side void warehouse (carpet-Neko-Addition) instead of relying on carried shulker boxes.
Requires carpet-Neko-Addition on the server with both the §bvoidWarehouse§r and §bvoidWarehouseRestock§r Carpet rules enabled. If the server has it disabled, the request fails immediately instead of being retried every tick.
Count Void Warehouse Stock in Material List

"Available" in the material list becomes player inventory + void warehouse, so the missing list only keeps what the warehouse cannot supply either - you can see at a glance what still needs gathering.
Shares the same server capability as restocking: requires carpet-Neko-Addition on the server with both the §bvoidWarehouse§r and §bvoidWarehouseRestock§r Carpet rules enabled.
Queries every 5 seconds while the material list screen or the material info HUD is open; backs off to once a minute when the server has it disabled, and recovers automatically once it is turned on.

Restocking hands out a whole stack, so half-used stacks keep occupying inventory slots. Once a build needs many block types, those leftovers fill every slot and no new material can come in.
When enabled: leftovers go back in bulk once printing stops (§bwork switch off§r); while printing, a batch is returned once §b3 or fewer slots are free§r, topping the free slots back up to 8.
The trigger only looks at whether new material still fits, and it only acts when the inventory actually holds §ewarehouse-supplied items§r - your own stacks are never touched. Materials currently being requested are skipped, so nothing is returned only to be fetched again.
Shares the same server capability as restocking: carpet-Neko-Addition with both the §bvoidWarehouse§r and §bvoidWarehouseRestock§r Carpet rules enabled.
litematic-printer-ling.config.cacheSelec: Hotkey: add Chest Tracker remembered containers inside the current Litematica AreaSelection to the local remote-take allow-list.
litematic-printer-ling.config.clearConta: Hotkey: clear the cached remote-take containers for the current world and dimension.
litematic-printer-ling.config.missingMat: Show materials that block printing, filling, or fluid removal in the unified printer HUD. Supplied materials disappear automatically.
Display current mode and work progress within range on operation page when printer is working;
If §6§lLag Detection§r is enabled, will show prompt when lag is excessive.
litematic-printer-ling.config.renderHudX: Set the X position of the unified printer HUD.
litematic-printer-ling.config.renderHudY: Set the Y position of the unified printer HUD.
litematic-printer-ling.config.renderHudS: Set the overall scale percentage of the unified printer HUD.
litematic-printer-ling.hud.missing.title: Missing materials: %s types
litematic-printer-ling.config.storeOrder: Near a full inventory, return the least recently used Quick Shulker items and clean up idle items automatically; prefer the original shulker and slot, then matching stacks and empty slots.
litematic-printer-ling.config.switchPrin: Switch printer's current work mode (printing/mining/bedrock breaking, etc.).
litematic-printer-ling.config.unlockBeac:
Relax the client-side beacon UI effect tier limits and allow selecting primary/secondary effects that would normally be unavailable at the current beacon level, similar to wacko-beacons.
This does not change server-side validation; whether it actually works depends on the server still being vulnerable or unpatched.
litematic-printer-ling.config.scanTimeBu:
Main-thread time cap for the entry scanner per tick, in milliseconds.
This is a safety fuse, not a performance optimization switch. Raising it only allows more same-tick scanning and may stutter; lowering it yields earlier to the next tick and may refresh targets more slowly.
litematic-printer-ling.config.lazyEnterT: Number of continuously idle ticks before the entry scanner enters lazy state; 0 disables lazy scanning.
Printer's maximum work radius centered on player (blocks). Larger values mean wider coverage.
This parameter is associated with §6§lIteration Area Shape§r.

litematic-printer-ling.config.syncInvent:
Use the pointed container as a slot-by-slot template for matching chests, barrels, shulker boxes, hoppers, dispensers, droppers or crafters in the area selection.
Crafters sync items only, preserving target disabled slots and pausing on conflicts (requires a Minecraft version with crafters).
Requires the master switch and an empty main hand. Surplus returns to inventory; missing items or space pauses the task.
